clinicalPearls: Term for severe deficiency of high-density lipoprotein, in which plasma HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A-I are extremely low or absent
Includes ABCA1-related Tangier disease and forms caused by variants in APOA1, the gene encoding the principal HDL apolipoprotein
Shares clinical features with Tangier disease, including very low HDL and total cholesterol, hepatosplenomegaly, and in some cases enlarged lipid-laden tonsils
Peripheral neuropathy can occur and may be relapsing and multifocal or produce a syringomyelia-like dissociated sensory loss with preferential loss of pain and temperature sensation
Certain APOA1 variants also cause hereditary systemic amyloidosis with organ deposition, adding to the phenotypic range
A markedly reduced HDL cholesterol on a routine lipid panel is the key laboratory clue and should prompt further evaluation when accompanied by neuropathy or organomegaly
Diagnosis combines the characteristic lipid abnormalities with genetic testing of ABCA1 and APOA1
reference.pathophysiology: Analphalipoproteinaemia describes states of profound high-density lipoprotein deficiency arising from defects in HDL metabolism. In ABCA1-related disease (Tangier disease), impaired cholesterol efflux prevents lipidation of apolipoprotein A-I, which is then rapidly degraded; in APOA1-related disease, variants reduce or abolish functional apolipoprotein A-I itself. Either mechanism leaves the body unable to assemble normal HDL particles, so HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A-I are very low and cholesterol accumulates within tissue macrophages, producing hepatosplenomegaly and, in some cases, lipid-laden tonsils. Deposition of lipid within Schwann cells and peripheral nerves is thought to drive the neuropathy, which can be multifocal and relapsing or cause a pseudosyringomyelic dissociated sensory loss. Some APOA1 variants additionally form amyloid deposits.
additionalDifferentials: Tangier disease (as a specific ABCA1 cause)
Secondary causes of low HDL (severe illness, drugs, metabolic syndrome)
additionalInvestigations: Fasting lipid panel demonstrating very low HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A-I
Sequencing of ABCA1 and APOA1 to define the molecular cause
Nerve conduction studies to characterise the neuropathy
Assessment for hepatosplenomegaly and lipid deposition in tonsils
Evaluation for systemic amyloidosis where an APOA1 amyloidogenic variant is suspected
Cardiovascular risk assessment in view of altered HDL-mediated protection
redFlags: Rapidly progressive multifocal neuropathy causing significant disability
Features of systemic amyloidosis such as renal or hepatic involvement with APOA1 variants
Progressive dissociated sensory loss raising concern for a spinal cord lesion
Painless burns or injuries from unrecognised loss of pain and temperature sensation
reference.prognosis: Variable and dependent on the underlying gene; neuropathy can be disabling, and APOA1-related amyloidosis may affect vital organs and thereby prognosis, while cardiovascular risk is also altered by the HDL deficiency.
pitfalls: Dismissing a very low HDL as laboratory error rather than a diagnostic clue
Failing to distinguish ABCA1 (Tangier) from APOA1-related disease, which can cause amyloidosis
Mistaking pseudosyringomyelic sensory loss for a primary cord lesion
Overlooking secondary causes of low HDL before pursuing a genetic diagnosis
references: GeneReviews / OMIM: APOA1- and ABCA1-Related HDL Deficiency
Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Recognise that no specific therapy restores the deficient high-density lipoprotein, so care is supportive and directed at complications
Modify cardiovascular risk through control of other lipids, blood pressure and glycaemia and through smoking cessation
Manage the peripheral neuropathy with neuropathic pain agents, physiotherapy and functional support
Monitor for systemic amyloidosis where an amyloidogenic APOA1 variant is present, assessing affected organs
Assess periodically for hepatosplenomegaly and lipid deposition
Confirm the molecular cause by sequencing ABCA1 and APOA1 and offer genetic counselling and family screening
Coordinate care across neurology and lipid specialist services
